title: Not sorted interfaces in config_db.json file
author: Hedgehog-Guru
body:
**Description**

Not sorted interface in config_db.json file. In the previous builds, the configuration file was readable and sorted but for now it like some randomly generated and not sorted content, it is very hard to read, search and troubleshoot something manually there.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Run more /etc/sonic/config_db.json
2. Observer unsorted interfaces in the configuration file

comments.author: liat-grozovik
tahmed-dev
comments.body: Thanks @Hedgehog-Guru , @liat-grozovik . The sorting of config_db file was remove via commit [9122d16d](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/commit/9122d16dd28c36d10a05ce0b30d81ff6273f1c63). The sorting logic was mainly used in unit test to compare outputs as strings and so the need for the string to be sorted. Since `natsort` cause almost 1s during run-time and there is no requirement to have config_db sorted (might be useful for manual diffs,) `natsort` was removed and the verification logic is moved to the unit tests. Please let me know if you further concerns. If not, I'd recommend closing this issue.

comments.author: Hedgehog-Guru
comments.body:
Dear @tahmed-dev, in this particular case, I think the problem is extremely critical. The operating system for a network engineer is CLI and configuration files.
SONiC, as an operating system is designed not only for automated deployment, but also for network engineers to work with it, as evidenced by the presence of the command line, and configuration files are the result of commands. Of the hardware and operating systems presented in the top segment for it, I have never encountered that configuration files were not sorted. Unsorted configuration files and command results result in huge configuration costs.
I strongly recommend, from the point of view of the network engineer, to return the sorting of the configuration file. Let's not ruin the attitude of network engineers to work with the SONiC operating system.

comments.author: liat-grozovik
comments.body:
I totally agree.
Although SONiC upstream code removed as explained there are users who expect to have it sorted for easily use and tracking.
I strongly vote for having that back.
Also there is non public automation and validations that end users have internally so I do think this will break it for them as well.
